To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
variant 3' tail regions of U1 RNA precursors are expressed in He La cells and are transcribed by RNA polymerase II.
the variant 3' tail of the U1 RNA is expressed in human cells, and that the variant tail sequence contains a putative Sm antigen-binding site.
variant 3' U1 flanking sequences are expressed in human cells and contain the putative A(U)3-G binding site.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transcription of U1 precursor sequences.
the transcription and splicing of the small nuclear ribonucleoprotein (snRNP) genes.
the transcription of the 3'-flanking sequences of U1 genes in human cells, and with the possible functional role of these flanking sequences in the assembly of the U1 ribonucleoprotein particle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 3' end of U1 RNA is generated in human cells by transcription of a subset of 3' tail sequence elements, and that the U1 3'-end processing mechanism may not be the same in all eucaryotic organisms.
U1 precusor tails are transcribed and that they contain the Sm binding site.
U1 precursers are derived from transcription of variant 3' tail flanking sequences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
U1 precusors are generated by transcription of 5' and 3' flanked sequences.
U1 precursers are derived from transcription of 3 flanking sequences, and that variant U1 5' tails are expressed in human cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the U1 gene locus is transcribed as a single precursor, which contains all the information necessary to produce all of the mature U1 RNA isoforms.
the 3' end of human U1 RNA is not derived from a unique 3' processing signal, as is the case with U1 RNA from Xenopus laevis.
the 3' tail of the U1 RNA is derived by transcription of flanking sequences and is not a result of RNA processing.
